narrative_purpose: Contrasts the two ends of the abundance-versus-size rule in one landscape: the solitary giant flier that lives and dies where nothing accumulates, and the dense herd that dies beside a delta that is actively burying things. It makes visible why the record will over-represent the second and effectively miss the first.
subject: A single tall landscape composition. In the upper portion, one enormous solitary winged predator soars alone above a bare, sharply eroding mountain ridge whose thin soil is visibly sliding and washing downslope in pale runnels, no sediment gathering anywhere. In the lower portion, a dense scattered herd of perhaps thirty small six-limbed grazers stands and lies along the margin of a broad river delta, where fine pale sediment is visibly accumulating in flat stacked layers and a shallow channel spills silt across a mudflat. One grazer carcass lies part-submerged in that fresh silt.
scene: A vertically stacked Pandoran landscape at dusk: barren high ridge above, fertile depositional lowland delta below, deep atmospheric haze separating the two elevations.
camera: A tall vertical view taking in both elevations at once, the ridge occupying the upper third and the delta the lower half, the flier small against the sky to convey solitude.
light: Dim bioluminescent ambience from the lowland vegetation glowing cool teal on the wet silt; the high ridge cold, cyan-grey, unlit from within; one restrained warm amber accent on the solitary flier so the eye finds it first.
palette: Cool teal and cyan across the delta, cold grey-indigo on the eroding ridge, one scarce ember-amber highlight on the flier.
style: Painterly naturalist landscape plate, hand-painted texture, observed rather than dramatised.
detail_level: Crisp on the delta's layered sediment, the silt-buried carcass, and the erosion runnels on the ridge; the flier crisp in silhouette; the middle distance dissolving into haze.
composition: Strong vertical stack with a hazy separation band, the lone flier high and isolated against dark sky with clear space around it, the herd dense and low, generous quiet areas for later callouts.
consistency_notes: Six limbs on every grazer. Exactly one flier, to convey low density. Sediment must visibly accumulate in the lowland and visibly wash away on the ridge - the contrast between depositional and erosional is the whole figure.
